The new tetrahedron is formed by replacing the LRU vertex of the previous tetrahedron with $v_k$, effectively shifting the vertex window by one position [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly defines a 'sequential strip' as a strip where 'the new vertex always replaces the least-recently-used (LRU) vertex of the previous tetrahedron.' Furthermore, the API description and code examples for `GL_SEQUENTIAL_TET_STRIP_EXT` demonstrate that each subsequent vertex replaces the first vertex of the previous tetrahedron (e.g., v5 replaces v1 in v1-v2-v3-v4 to form v2-v3-v4-v5), which corresponds to shifting the vertex window by one position.
